gen.subtitle: Generator
gen.catalogBody: LovyanGFX already ships with 186 fonts, and using one costs no flash for glyph data at all. Generate here when you want a size or a typeface the presets do not have, or when you want to pay flash for only the characters you actually use.
gen.catalogLink: Browse the 186 built-in fonts in the Viewer →
gen.googleNote: Only SIL OFL 1.1 and Apache-2.0 families are listed — both allow the generated glyph data to be embedded in and shipped with your firmware (with attribution, which the generated header carries).
gen.localWarnTitle: Check the licence before you use this.
gen.localWarnBody: Generating an embedded font converts the typeface's glyphs into data that ships inside your firmware — that is redistribution. Many fonts, including most commercial fonts and the ones bundled with Windows, macOS and Office, do not permit it. Only use a file here if its licence explicitly allows embedding and redistribution.
gen.sizeNote: The size is the character height in pixels — the ink height of a reference glyph (an ideograph for CJK-capable fonts, a capital otherwise), so "24" looks the same size in every typeface. The line height is derived from the glyphs and reported next to the preview. Output is 1bpp: the threshold decides how much anti-aliased coverage counts as "on"; lowering it makes the font heavier.
gen.customPlaceholder: Paste any characters you also need…
gen.showCharsNote: Grouped by code point — use the browser's find (Ctrl+F) to check a specific character.
gen.previewNote: Rendered from the generated 1bpp glyphs with the library's LovyanGFX-exact engine — this is exactly what the device will draw.
gen.codeNote: Showing the first {shown} of {total} lines — download for the whole file.
gen.howto: How to use the generated header
cv.subtitle: Converter
cv.inputNote: Drop in a font file — u8g2 / GFX1 container / BDF / VLW / BFF / FONTX2 binaries, or a C/C++ header with GFXfont or u8g2 data in it. The format is detected from the content; override it below if the guess is wrong.
in.subtitle: Inspector
in.firstOfMany: The file contains {count} fonts — showing the first (use the Converter to pick).
in.textCheckNote: Paste the strings your device will display — anything the font cannot draw is listed by character.
in.sizesNote: Exact byte counts from the real encoders (violating glyphs dropped where necessary) — use this to pick the output format before converting.
home.tagline: Read, convert, render and generate embedded bitmap fonts — in the browser.
home.lead: Decoders and encoders for u8g2 / GFXfont / BDF / VLW / BFF / FONTX2, a text renderer that matches LovyanGFX pixel for pixel, and all 186 fonts built into LovyanGFX v1.2.26. Everything below runs entirely in your browser — no install, and your font files never leave your machine.
home.viewerDesc: Browse the 186 built-in LovyanGFX fonts and preview any text exactly as the device will draw it — scaling, datum and grid included.
home.generatorDesc: Turn a TTF or a redistributable Google Font into a u8g2 / GFXfont header: pick the exact characters, fill gaps from a fallback typeface, download a .h with attribution included.
home.converterDesc: Drop in a font file or a C header — the format is auto-detected — and convert it to any other format, with constraint violations reported instead of silent truncation.
home.inspectorDesc: Inventory any font: metrics, code point ranges, coverage per character set, "can it draw my strings?" checks, and exact size in every output format.
home.libDesc: Everything these pages do is a plain-ESM JavaScript library with zero runtime dependencies — npm install lgfx-font-tool, or import it from a CDN. Rendering is verified byte-exact against the real LovyanGFX on 1,860 oracle cases.
